title: Extension by zero commutes with $T$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings, with derived
extensions of scalars $T^X$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]), let $X$ and $U$ be schemes, and let
$j\colon U\to X$ be an open immersion. The natural isomorphism

$$
T^X\circ D(j_!)\;\cong\;D(j_!)\circ T^U\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})\longrightarrow
D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X})
$$

on the unbounded derived categories, with $D(j_!)$ the levelwise extension by zero
([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]), is the conjugate ([def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso]) of the
isomorphism $D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_U})\circ D(j^*)\cong D(j^*)\circ D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$
of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] along the adjunctions $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$
([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]) and $T\dashv D(\operatorname{Res})$
([sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]). No flatness of $a$ is needed.

proof.text: For each coefficient ring $B=\Lambda,\Lambda'$, the exact extension by zero $j_!^B$ and its adjunction $j_!^B\dashv j_B^*$ are supplied by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Write $F_B=D(j_!^B)$ and $G_B=D(j_B^*)$. Here $D$ is localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms, using only the opening unbounded-localization convention of the current [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Its conditional assertions about resolution-computed derived functors are not needed: we construct the termwise functor directly as follows. To construct $F_B$ without any resolution hypotheses, apply exactness of $j_!^B$ to $0\to Z^nC\to C^n\to B^{n+1}C\to0$ and $0\to B^nC\to Z^nC\to H^nC\to0$. These exact sequences identify the cycles and boundaries of $j_!^BC$ with $j_!^BZ^nC$ and $j_!^BB^nC$, and give $H^n(j_!^BC)\cong j_!^BH^n(C)$, naturally in $C$. Consequently termwise $j_!^B$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Let $Q_U^B,Q_X^B$ be the cochain localization functors defining the unbounded derived categories. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $Q_X^B\circ\mathrm{CoCh}(j_!^B)$: it sends every quasi-isomorphism to an isomorphism, so it descends to $F_B$ with its termwise factorization isomorphism. The termwise pullbacks $G_\Lambda,G_{\Lambda'}$, including their factorization isomorphisms, are the functors appearing in [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] specialized to $f=j$. Apply the underived adjunction degreewise to cochain complexes: its natural unit $\eta^B$ and counit $\varepsilon^B$ are chain maps, since their naturality equations applied to each differential are exactly the chain-map equations. The two triangle identities hold in each degree. With the termwise factorization identifications, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends $Q_U^B\eta^B$ to $\bar\eta^B:1\to G_BF_B$ and $Q_X^B\varepsilon^B$ to $\bar\varepsilon^B:F_BG_B\to1$. On $Q_U^BC$ and $Q_X^BE$, respectively, the composites $\bar\varepsilon^B_{F_B(-)}\circ F_B(\bar\eta^B)$ and $G_B(\bar\varepsilon^B)\circ\bar\eta^B_{G_B(-)}$ are the images of the degreewise triangle identities, hence identities. Clause (3) of the same localization statement makes these identities of natural transformations on the whole derived categories. Thus these descended maps define $F_B\dashv G_B$, precisely the ambient levelwise adjunction required in the statement.

Descent expanded by lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property: Stacks Tag 04VG, categories.tex, lemma-properties-left-localization (3), for functor descent; natural-transformation descent and equality detection are the fully faithful precomposition formulation, as in Mathlib CategoryTheory/Localization/Predicate.lean:278-292.

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso] with $\mathcal A=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, $\mathcal B=D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X})$, $\mathcal A'=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})$, and $\mathcal B'=D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_U})$. Set $E_1=T^X$, $E_2=T^U$, $\mathrm{Res}_1=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$, $\mathrm{Res}_2=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_U})$, $U_1=F_\Lambda$, $U_2=F_{\Lambda'}$, $L_1=G_\Lambda$ and $L_2=G_{\Lambda'}$. The two coefficient adjunctions are part of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] (equivalently the derived extension/restriction adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]); the two open adjunctions are step 1. The isomorphism of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] for $f=j$ is exactly $e:\mathrm{Res}_2L_2\cong L_1\mathrm{Res}_1$. Its conjugate therefore has source $E_1U_1=T^X D(j_!^\Lambda)$ and target $U_2E_2=D(j_!^{\Lambda'})T^U$. Define the comparison in this node to be that conjugate. This specifies the actual natural isomorphism, not merely its existence. All four categories are unbounded, and none of the cited inputs assumes flatness of $a$; hence the construction requires no such hypothesis.
